title: Latency burn and threshold playbook
content:
Purpose:
A compact, spreadsheet-style playbook to track latency-related KPIs across rollout phases and to define automatic/manual mitigations when latency 'burn' approaches SLO thresholds. Designed for product-ops + infra + serving-runtime handoff during pilot -> scale.

How to use this sheet:
- Maintain one row per (phase, route, model-variant) combination.
- Alerting should map to the Warning and Critical triggers below.
- Owners are expected to annotate status in the "status" column during launches.

MASTER TABLE (columns): Phase | Route / Model | KPI | Metric | Baseline (now) | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Detection window | Trigger condition | Automated mitigation | Manual mitigation | Owner | Escalation ticket | Rollback criteria | Status

Rows:
1) Canary | text-gen / rwd-13b-v1 | Latency (p95) | ms | 85 | 160 | 350 | 5m | p95 > 160ms for 5m | autoscale + reduce batching by 20% | Route 60% traffic to rwd-7b-fallback; open incident; run quick eval | Diego Ramos | PRODOPS-421 | p95 > 350ms sustained 3m -> immediate traffic cut to fallback | monitoring

2) Beta (10% traffic) | embeddings / rwd-embed-v2 | Tail tokens (max latency per token) | ms/token | 12 | 22 | 50 | 10m | 95th-tail per-request token-latency > 22ms | enable per-route prefix cache; increase KV cache retention | Memory+cache review; possible canary rollback | Maya Liu | PRODOPS-433 | Critical -> roll back to host-only embedding pool | staging

3) Dedicated (reserved pool) | chat / rwd-13b-quant | Cost-per-1k-tokens + Latency (p50,p95) | $/1k, ms | $1.6 / 42 / 95 | $2.2 / 70 / 180 | $3.5 / 120 / 400 | 30m | unit-cost > $2.2 OR p95 > 180ms | switch to quantized kernels profile B; reduce max_tokens default by 25% | Trigger dedicated capacity increase request; pause non-critical background batch jobs | Samir Khatri | PRODOPS-450 | Cost spike + p95 breach -> pause new customer onboarding traffic | ready-for-canary

4) Private (VPC customer) | all routes | SLA adherence | % requests within p95 SLO | 99.2% | 97.5% | 95% | 60m | rolling 1h window below 97.5% | failover to cross-region private pool; enable degraded-mode that disables heavy tool-calls | Contact account eng/CS; coordinate dedicated escalation | Aisha Patel | PRODOPS-460 | sustained <95% -> emergency maintenance window + rollback to previous model commit | review

Derived KPI panel (formulas / notes):
- p95 latency = percentile(95, request.latency_ms) over 5m windows per route
- Latency burn rate = (current SLO shortfall seconds per hr) / (allowed budget seconds per hr) -> used as early warning
- Cost per 1k tokens = (compute_cost + infra_overhead) / (tokens_processed / 1000) – maintained per-model-variant daily

Ramp knobs (what Product Ops can adjust quickly):
- Traffic weight (canary % -> full rollout)
- Model variant route (13b -> 7b fallback -> distilled tiny)
- Batch size and aggregation window (server knob)
- Max response tokens default override per route
- Persistent KV cache TTL per customer prefix
- Kernel/profile selection (quantization profile A/B/C)

Runbook snippets (copy-paste into PagerDuty incident notes):
1) Detection: "p95 > 160ms for rwd-13b-v1 on canary for 5m"
2) Automated actions already taken: "Reduced batch window 20%; enabled autoscale step +1"
3) Tasks for oncall:
   - Confirm CPU/GPU saturation via infra dashboards (metric links)
   - Check model compilation errors or kernel fallbacks in serving logs (grep for kernel_mismatch)
   - If p95 remains > critical -> execute manual traffic shift play: /ops shift-route --route rwd-13b-v1 --to rwd-7b-fallback --pct 60
   - Notify product + CS if user-impacting (customer-visible errors)

Slack channels and stakeholders:
- #prodops-latency (primary)
- #serving-runtime (gpu/kernel issues)
- #cs-accounts (when private customers impacted)
- Escalation list: Diego Ramos -> Maya Liu -> Aisha Patel -> VP Product Ops

Open questions and TODOs:
- How to surface cross-customer prefix cache collisions in our traces? (ACTION: infra instrumentation spike, owner: Samir)
- Define exact cost-accounting mapping for Dedicated pools (ACTION: finance sync, owner: Maya)
- Add a simpler 'health index' (0-100) to show combined latency+error+cost on a single tile for exec readouts (ACTION: product-ops prototype, owner: Aisha)

Next steps before formalizing into launch runbook:
- Wire these rows to Grafana alerting (list of panel ids in linked_artifacts)
- Create Linear ticket to centralize mitigation scripts (/ops helpers) and stash the runbook commands in repo
- Run a tabletop drill with SRE + serving-runtime to validate manual shift command and rollback time (~10m target)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the warning threshold conservative early; we want more noisy alerts during canary than silent failures in GA.
- Don't forget to test quantized profile C with short sequence length before ramping up traffic (compilation regressions sometimes surface).

Revision history:
- 2024-10-21 created by Aisha Patel (initial scaffold)
- 2024-10-28 added Dedicated and Private rows after infra sync (Samir)
- 2024-11-05 tuned thresholds following tabletop drill (Diego)

Attachments & references:
- Confluence: latency-burnbook (see linked_artifacts)
- Example Grafana alert expressions: avg_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))) > 0.16
- Quick commands: /ops shift-route --help | /ops kernel-switch --profile B
